## Discovery & Translational Science

- **[AAV8 gene therapy demonstrates hepatobiliary safety in large animals](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42958795/)** — *PubMed*
  - Large animal preclinical models receiving AAV8-based gene therapy for X-linked myotubular myopathy showed a complete absence of hepatobiliary toxicity.

- **[Novel small-molecule chimera selectively drives mitophagy in damaged mitochondria](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42958763/)** — *PubMed*
  - Researchers developed a damage-gated small-molecule chimera that couples dysfunctional mitochondria to autophagy machinery, selectively promoting mitophagy without affecting intact organelles.

- **[Acute alcohol exposure induces selective plasma FGF21 elevation](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.27.762218)** — *bioRxiv*
  - A proteomic analysis of 1,462 plasma proteins following acute ethanol ingestion identified Fibroblast Growth Factor 21 (FGF21) as a uniquely responsive endocrine biomarker in humans.
  - The findings provide biomarker context for ongoing Phase 2 clinical trials testing FGF21 analogues in metabolic dysfunction and alcohol-related liver disease.

- **[LITMUS study identifies proteomic panels for non-invasive MASH diagnosis](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01145-1/fulltext)** — *The Lancet*
  - Results from the prospective multicenter LITMUS study evaluated non-invasive tests (NITs) against liver histology in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
  - While single markers performed poorly in detecting at-risk metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), a novel multi-marker proteomic panel demonstrated superior accuracy in identifying significant (≥F2) fibrosis.

- **[Physicochemical rule-embedded generative model optimizes constrained peptide design](https://www.nature.com/articles/s44386-026-00090-1)** — *npj Drug Discovery*
  - A generative machine learning framework integrating explicit physicochemical constraints was introduced to accelerate the de novo design of structurally stable, constrained peptide therapeutics.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

- **[Biotech]** **[Small-molecule TREM2 agonist VG-3927 shows CNS penetration in Phase 1](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41591-026-00055-x)** — *Nature Medicine*
  - Preclinical and Phase 1 trial data evaluating VG-3927, an oral small-molecule TREM2 agonist for Alzheimer’s disease, confirmed successful blood-brain barrier penetration.
  - The compound demonstrated clear target engagement in the central nervous system alongside a favorable clinical safety and tolerability profile.

- **[MEK 1/2 inhibitor EDV2209 meets safety endpoints in subarachnoid hemorrhage](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42957924/)** — *PubMed*
  - A first-in-human Phase 1b/2a trial demonstrated that EDV2209, an investigational MEK 1/2 inhibitor, was safe and well-tolerated in patients with spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage.

- **[IL-4Rα blockade yields proof-of-concept in localized scleroderma](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42957460/)** — *PubMed*
  - A Phase 2 proof-of-concept trial demonstrated clinical activity and safety following targeted interleukin-4 receptor-α (IL-4Rα) inhibition in patients with localized scleroderma.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **[Biotech]** **[Genmab’s petosemtamab combination reduces death risk by 50% in Phase 3 HNSCC trial](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/genmab-stock-soars-positive-head-neck-cancer-antibody-phase-3/873164/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - Genmab announced positive Phase 3 results combining petosemtamab with Keytruda as a first-line treatment for PD-L1-positive head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC).
  - An interim analysis showed the combination halved the risk of death compared to Keytruda monotherapy, successfully meeting dual primary endpoints for overall response rate and overall survival.
  - Genmab plans to submit the data to global regulatory authorities as it seeks to build revenue ahead of Darzalex patent expirations.

- **[Phase 3 PROSpect trial shows no benefit for prone positioning or HFOV in pediatric ARDS](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01949-5/fulltext)** — *The Lancet*
  - The international Phase 3 PROSpect trial evaluated high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) and prone positioning in early moderate-to-severe pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS).
  - Neither strategy improved ventilator-free days compared to standard care, leading researchers to recommend against their routine first-line use in this setting.

## Regulatory & Approvals

- **[HHS permits compounding of six unapproved peptides despite FDA objections](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/hhs-peptides-rfk-fda-compounders/873141/)** — *BioPharma Dive / [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/29/biotech-news-hhs-green-lights-six-peptides-for-now/)*
  - HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. issued a Federal Register notice stating the department will exercise enforcement discretion allowing licensed pharmacies and physicians to compound six unapproved peptides.
  - The policy bypasses career FDA scientists, who refused to endorse safety regulations for the substances due to potential clinical risks.

- **[Labor Department finalizes mandatory PBM fee disclosure rule](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/pbm-transparency-final-rule-labor-department-employer/873254/)** — *BioPharma Dive / [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/29/prescription-drug-price-reform-pbm-disclosure-rules-face-challenge/)*
  - A final Department of Labor rule requires pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) to disclose detailed compensation, manufacturer rebates, and spread pricing data to self-insured employer plans.
  - Taking effect in July 2027, the semi-annual reporting mandates are projected by federal regulators to save employers $22 billion over ten years.

- **[FDA updates QT/QTc evaluation guidance under ICH E14 and S7B](http://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/e14-and-s7b-clinical-and-nonclinical-evaluation-qtqtc-interval-prolongation)** — *FDA*
  - FDA finalized the Q&A (R1) revision updating the ICH E14 and S7B guidances on clinical and nonclinical evaluation of QT/QTc interval prolongation and proarrhythmic potential.
  - Revisions clarify clinical testing strategies in Questions 5.1, 6.1, and 6.3 for E14 and update nonclinical assay and integrated risk assessment recommendations in Sections 1 and 3 for S7B.
  - Additional newly finalized FDA guidances cover clinical trial data submission for motor vehicle operation, prescription drug use-related software, and post-approval manufacturing changes for biosimilars.

- **[FDA conducts engagement webinar on ICH M15 model-informed drug development guideline](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/webinar-stakeholder-engagement-new-final-guideline-general-principles-model-informed-drug)** — *FDA*
  - The agency held a stakeholder webinar detailing the implementation of the final ICH M15 guideline, General Principles for Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD).
  - The guideline establishes a harmonized international assessment framework, standardized terminology, and recommendations for model evaluation and documentation to support regulatory evidence.

## Business & Strategy

- **[Big Pharma]** **[Eli Lilly beats Q3 estimates and hikes full-year revenue guidance by $5B](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/biopharma-earnings-q3-2026-lilly-novartis-gsk/873167/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - Eli Lilly reported Q3 revenue 8% above consensus forecasts, driven by strong demand for its GLP-1 therapies Mounjaro and Zepbound.
  - Management raised full-year sales guidance by $5 billion, alleviating investor concerns regarding GLP-1 market price shifts and Medicare Bridge program impacts.

- **[Biotech]** **[Aspen Neuroscience completes $141M IPO for autologous Parkinson's cell therapy](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/aspen-neuroscience-parkinsons-ipo-pricing/873050/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - Aspen Neuroscience priced its IPO at $15 per share, raising $140.6 million to fund clinical development of sasineprocel under ticker symbol ASPE.
  - Sasineprocel is a personalized, skin-cell-derived cell therapy designed to replace destroyed dopamine-producing neurons in Parkinson's disease.

- **[Big Pharma]** **[Regeneron beats Q3 expectations as Eylea HD sales reach $699M](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2116119108030972222)** — *BioStocks on X*
  - Regeneron reported Q3 EPS of $20.07 on total revenue of $5.1B, outperforming consensus estimates of $16.19 EPS and $4.5B in sales.
  - U.S. net sales of high-dose aflibercept (Eylea HD) increased 62% to $699M, while legacy Eylea U.S. net sales dropped 41% to $400M.

- **[Biotech]** **[Aurinia reports 12% growth in Q3 Lupkynis sales to $79.4M](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2116139475935850706)** — *BioStocks on X*
  - Net product sales of voclosporin (Lupkynis) increased 12% year-over-year to $79.4M.
  - The company closed the quarter with $487M in cash and cash equivalents and repurchased 5M shares for $74.9M.

- **[Biotech]** **[Repligen announces $1B private convertible note offering](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2116108491416907813)** — *BioStocks on X*
  - Repligen announced a $1B private placement of convertible senior notes.

## Public Health & Policy

- **[Federal judge overturns restricted Medicaid "medical frailty" definition](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/29/medicaid-work-requirements-judge-blocks-new-limits-medical-frailty/)** — *STAT*
  - A federal judge ruled that health regulators exceeded statutory authority when narrowing the medical frailty definition used to exempt vulnerable individuals from Medicaid work requirements.

- **[FDA and CMS negotiate to align federal rules with state clinical AI testbeds](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/30/fda-cms-health-ai-regulation-state-sandboxes-run-into-federal-rules/)** — *STAT*
  - Federal regulators are coordinating with state-level health "sandboxes" to streamline oversight and avoid regulatory conflicts over the deployment of artificial intelligence systems in clinical settings.

- **[The Lancet Men's Health Series outlines global mortality burden and governance gaps](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01490-X/fulltext?rss=yes)** — *The Lancet*
  - Analysis of Global Burden of Disease data (1990–2023) highlights lower life expectancy and higher disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) in males, with disproportionate impact on marginalized populations.
  - Authors advocate for an intersectional governance framework to address long-standing gaps in national and global health policy agendas.

- **[Lancet Viewpoint positions online "manosphere" as a public health determinant](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)02027-1/fulltext?rss=yes)** — *The Lancet*
  - Viewpoint authors categorize the commercial ecosystem of male-victimhood online communities as an under-recognized determinant of health harms.
  - Key harms cited include youth mental health strain, gender-based violence, and diminished healthcare help-seeking among men and boys.

**Worth watching:** Genmab's upcoming global regulatory submissions for petosemtamab as the company moves to build revenue ahead of Darzalex patent expirations.

- Pure Science
    - [What if We Can't Detect Dark Matter?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QXXqSh5qAuA) -- minutephysics
        - The video examines popular theoretical candidates for dark matter, including Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs), axions, Massive Astrophysical Compact Halo Objects (MACHOs), and Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) / modified gravity.
        - It details observational evidence for dark matter, including galactic rotation curves, gravitational lensing, cosmic microwave background radiation anisotropies, and large-scale cosmic web structure.
        - It discusses a theoretical "nightmare scenario" regarding the direct detectability of dark matter particles.
        - The video features input from Prof. Vuk Mandic and Dr. Luna Zagorac as part of the "50x50: Science Across America" series highlighting Minnesota physics research.
    - [30 - Cookie  #mathctober](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/fVU-0Wq0UvE) -- El Jj
        - The video is entry 30 ("Cookie") in the channel's #mathctober mathematical challenge series.
        - It presents a mathematical optimization problem centered on helping a "cookie monster" devour a set of cookies.
        - The prompt challenges viewers to determine the optimal strategy or path to consume all cookies efficiently.
- Other
    - [How Geologists Can Tell if the World is Warming : Crash Course Geology #23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y5RqfQvCaBY) -- CrashCourse
        - The video explains how geological evidence from Earth's deep past is used to understand modern climate change dynamics.
        - It focuses on the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum (PETM), one of the hottest recorded periods in Earth's geological history.
        - It details the methods geologists use to detect and analyze historical temperature spikes like the PETM from the geological record.
        - It explores what the thermal and environmental responses during the PETM indicate about Earth's potential future warming trajectory.
